title: Generic shift and cone stability of dualizable derived objects
statement: Let $C$ be a braided monoidal closed [def-sfb-monoidal-category] Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor product, a derived category, and functorial flat resolutions. Give $D(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] its ordinary derived tensor. If $K$ admits a right dual, so does $K[n]$ for every integer $n$. If $T$ is a distinguished triangle and its first two objects admit right duals, so does its third object. Dualizability here means an evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities; it is the existing property $\operatorname{IsDualizable}$. These are the proved generic source-library theorems, with no finite-projective-unit hypothesis.

proof.text: The existing proved lemma DerivedCategory.isDualizable_shift writes the shifted object as a tensor product with the shifted unit; the shifted unit has the oppositely shifted unit as tensor inverse. Transport the tensor-product dual along the canonical shift comparison.

Use the existing proved theorem DerivedCategory.isDualizable_obj₃_of_distTriang. The natural map [K,1] tensor Z to [K,Z] is invertible for dualizable K; both functors take the rotated triangle to a distinguished triangle. The five lemma makes the third comparison invertible, and the closed-monoidal dualizability criterion supplies its dual.
